wave: REPRESENT-PROGRESSIVE-1: extent as a selection dimension
frozen: 2026-09-06, before any implementation, on main 1e57b6d1 (branch represent-progressive-1, worktree .claude/worktrees/represent-progressive-1)
lane: Semantic/plugin lane. The performance lane (K3 prefetch qualification, quantised banks, MLX, throughput) is PAUSED and nothing here measures time.
why: The codec contract declared extents on the day it was written and every codec registered since answers depth 0. `RepresentationExtent` is therefore a dimension the architecture claims and nothing exercises: no codec offers a second extent, no planner chooses one, no ledger prices one. This wave supplies the first codec with more than one extent and makes depth something the planner SELECTS under a budget — the first of the two hostile cases the contract must survive before it is frozen (the other is VQ's external codebook operand).

reconnaissance_2026_09_06.R1: `RepresentationExtent { depth }` and `ExtentCertificate { extent, bits_per_weight, radius: Option<ErrorRadius> }` already exist (`represent/codec/extent.rs`), with the progressive case written into the module's own doc comment. Every registered codec returns exactly one certificate, at TERMINAL.
reconnaissance_2026_09_06.R2: The trait already threads `extent` through `stored_bytes`, `validate`, `decode_rows`, `certificate_at` and `decode_all` (`represent/codec/mod.rs`). Admitting a progressive codec should require NO trait change — R2 is what P1 tests.
reconnaissance_2026_09_06.R3: `PlannedOperand.extent` exists (`opplan/planned.rs:103`) and is built `TERMINAL` unconditionally (`planned.rs:138`), which `opplan/tests/planned.rs:102` asserts. Nothing between the plan and the executor can express a different depth today.
reconnaissance_2026_09_06.R4: **The structural gap, as checked (this entry was corrected before any code was written — see R4_correction).** Two binding paths exist and neither takes an open set of streams. (a) Dense operands: `OperandStore::load` reads one `(object, tensor)` payload with one dtype (`exec/operands.rs:514`) and hands it to `decode_packed` → `bind_packed`, whose default REFUSES any codec declaring more than one stream (`codec/mod.rs`). (b) Bank operands: `experts.rs` loads `projection.weights` and an OPTIONAL `projection.scales`, and `lyrw2::bind_region` binds exactly those two as `VALUES` + `GROUP_SCALES` — a fixed two-slot shape, keyed to the scales role rather than to whatever the codec declares, always at `RepresentationExtent::TERMINAL`, and it enforces that the bound bytes total `stored_bytes(TERMINAL)` exactly. A progressive operand bound at depth 0 carries FEWER bytes than terminal, so that rule refuses it as a container/geometry disagreement. So 'physically separate refinement streams' forces two things into existence: binding N streams by their declared names, and a length rule stated per EXTENT rather than per tensor. MXFP4 becomes bindable through the general path as a side effect.
reconnaissance_2026_09_06.R4_correction: The first draft of R4 said no multi-stream binding existed at all. Checked against `experts.rs` and `codecs/lyrw2.rs` before any implementation: one does, for banks, with two hard-coded roles and a terminal-only length rule. The gap is narrower and more specific than the draft claimed, and the corrected R4 is what P2 is scored against.
reconnaissance_2026_09_06.R5: Selection: `select_realizations_within` (`exec/prepared.rs:1297`) re-selects greedily among a record's OWN candidates by declared resident saving, reason `BudgetPolicy`, and refuses before payload I/O with the irreducible deficit when nothing can be saved. Resources are `{stored, mapped, resident, transient, touch_per_token, page_in_per_token, device}` aggregated per dimension by `ResourceLedger::aggregate` (`exec/accounting.rs`). Extent is not a candidate axis.
reconnaissance_2026_09_06.R6: The precedent for 'executes through registration alone' is rung 2's BF16_ZLIB witness (`exec/tests/bf16_zlib_execution.rs`): two containers built from one fixture (`fixtures::{dense_f32_model, encode_bf16_zlib, encode_fixture_container}`) differing only in how the projections are stored, both executed through the plan, nothing under `exec/` outside `tests/` edited. This wave copies that shape.
reconnaissance_2026_09_06.R7: The out-of-tree acceptance test exists (`crates/larql-vindex/tests/external_codec_provider.rs`, rung 3d): a codec registered through exported API only, no core edits. A progressive codec must be addable the same way.

design.codec: `F32_PLANES` (family `F32_PLANES`, revision 1): byte-plane refinement of a row-major little-endian f32 image. Deliberately the simplest progressive scheme that is exact at the end — the planes PARTITION the source bytes, so nothing is stored twice and the terminal reconstruction is bit-identical by construction rather than by numerical argument.
extents: depth 0 — stream `base`: the high two bytes of each f32 (sign, exponent, 7 mantissa bits), truncated toward zero. 16 bits/weight.
depth 2 (TERMINAL) — `base` + `refine_1` + `refine_2`: the fourth byte. 32 bits/weight, the source f32 exactly.
design.fidelity: Truncation, so the error is one-sided and bounded by the bits discarded. A value is 1.m x 2^e with the significand in [1, 2): depth 0 keeps 7 stored mantissa bits, so the discarded residue is under one ulp of 2^-7 and the relative error is under 2^-7 (7.8e-3); depth 1 keeps 15, so under 2^-15 (3.1e-5); depth 2 is exact. The declared `ErrorRadius.relative_rms` is the uniform-residue RMS bound, 2^-7/sqrt(3) = 4.5e-3 and 2^-15/sqrt(3) = 1.8e-5, and 0 at terminal. Declared as a BOUND the codec is prepared to certify, and CHECKED (W5) rather than trusted — a one-sided error is exactly the case where a plausible-looking declaration can be wrong.
design.streams: `StreamRole::Refinement { depth }` joins Values/GroupScales/TensorScale — the first vocabulary extension the contract has needed since it was written, and in scope because the vocabulary is frozen AFTER progressive and VQ, not before. `base` keeps `StreamRole::Values`.
design.storage: The refinements are SIBLING TENSORS of the operand in the same object: `<tensor>` holds the base, `<tensor>.refine_1` and `<tensor>.refine_2` hold the planes. A depth-d decode reads exactly d+1 payloads and never opens the files above it — the witness is the store's own read ledger, not a flag.
design.no_direct_kernel: `accelerations()` returns empty. The codec executes through the mandatory canonical decode, which is the point: extent must be selectable without any kernel knowing it exists.
design.selection: Extent becomes a candidate axis beside the realization: for a codec declaring more than one extent, a record's candidates include the same realization at each ADMISSIBLE extent, and the existing greedy budget loop may descend depth exactly as it re-selects a cheaper realization, recording `SelectionReason::BudgetPolicy` with the certificate it chose. Admissibility comes from a declared fidelity floor carried by the budget (`RepresentationFloor`), defaulting to EXACT — so no existing plan changes behaviour, and a tight budget under the default REFUSES rather than quietly degrading quality.
design.which_budget_dimension_extent_moves: Derived during reconnaissance, before code, because it decides the shape of W1 and W3. Under the CANONICAL DECODE realization the resident image is f32 at every depth — decoding depth 0 still widens to four bytes a weight — so a shallower extent saves nothing on `resident` and everything on what is READ: `stored`, `touch_per_token`, `page_in_per_token`. Extent's value is therefore a property of the (representation x realization) PAIR, not of the representation alone, which is the four-plane thesis stated in the small. Two consequences: W1's budgets are THROUGHPUT budgets (bytes per token), not physical ones; and the greedy loop's switch metric must be the dimension actually in deficit rather than `resident` unconditionally — a generalisation of the existing rule, not a new algorithm, and explicitly NOT a quality optimiser. If a direct realization over the stored planes were ever added, resident would move with depth too; this wave does not add one.
design.boundary: No new selection ALGORITHM. The greedy policy proves deterministic feasibility, not optimal quality; the multi-resource quality choice belongs to REPRESENT and is not built here (the V2 boundary, restated). No timing claim, no direct kernel, no change to any existing codec's extents.

witnesses.W1_planner_chooses_depth: Three arms over one container, budgeted on THROUGHPUT (bytes per token — see `which_budget_dimension_extent_moves`): (a) generous budget, floor EXACT → terminal pinned; (b) tight budget, floor EXACT → refusal before payload I/O naming the deficit and the floor; (c) tight budget, floor 2^-7 → a shallower extent pinned, with the certificate and `BudgetPolicy` in the record. Different budgets, different depths, from the same plan.
witnesses.W2_depth_d_never_opens_above_d: A decode at depth d reads exactly d+1 payloads: asserted on the store's load count and touched-object set, AND by decoding at depth 0 and 1 from a container whose `refine_2` tensor is ABSENT, which must succeed while terminal refuses by name.
witnesses.W3_touch_moves_with_depth_and_resident_d: Read from `expectations`/`ResourceLedger`, not from the codec: `touch_per_token` and the stored bytes read at depth d are bits_per_weight(d)/bits_per_weight(terminal) of the terminal figures, while `resident` is unchanged because canonical decode widens to f32 at every depth. The container's stored footprint is also unchanged — the planes partition one object's bytes. A wave that reported resident falling with depth under a decode realization would be reporting a bug.
witnesses.W4_terminal_is_exact: Round-trip over an awkward fixture — non-power-of-two rows and columns, subnormals, ±0, the largest and smallest normals, and a NaN payload — is BIT-identical at depth 2. Values are compared as bit patterns, not as floats, so a NaN that changed payload is caught.
witnesses.W5_a_false_declaration_is_detected: A conformance harness decodes each extent, measures the error against the terminal decode, and refuses a codec whose measured relative RMS exceeds its declared radius or whose error does not fall with depth. The honest codec passes; a deliberately-lying control codec in the test — same bytes, radius declared 2^-16 at depth 0 — is caught and named.
witnesses.W6_execution_through_canonical_decode: Rung 2's shape: CONTROL container (the same fixture stored dense) and CANDIDATE (stored as planes) execute the same tokens through the plan, with identical logits at terminal depth, and nothing under `exec/` outside `tests/` edited for the candidate to run.
witnesses.W7_monotone: Measured error strictly decreases with depth on the fixture, and the declared radii are monotone in the same order — a certificate that improves while the decode does not is a defect this states as a test.
witnesses.W8_refusals_by_name: An extent above what the codec declares is refused as `ExtentUnavailable` (already in the vocabulary); a refinement stream missing at a depth that needs it is refused as `MissingStream` and never silently zero-filled; a floor no extent satisfies is refused before I/O naming the floor and the certificates that missed it.

predictions.P1: The `RepresentationCodec` trait needs NO shape change to admit a progressive codec. The edits land in four places instead: the stream-role vocabulary, a multi-stream binding path for vindex3 operands, extent-aware accounting, and extent as a selection axis. FALSIFIED if the trait's own signatures must change — which would mean the extent dimension was declared without being designed.
predictions.P2: R4's two blockers — binding streams by declared name, and a stored-length rule that is per-extent rather than terminal-only — are the ONLY structural ones between the contract and a multi-stream progressive codec, and closing them makes MXFP4 bindable through the general path. FALSIFIED if a third, independent blocker appears (for instance if a segment cannot carry sibling tensors of differing length, or if an operand cannot name its siblings to the loader).
predictions.P3: Depth selection needs no new selection algorithm: the existing greedy budget loop suffices once extents are candidates carrying declared resources. FALSIFIED if W1(c) cannot be made to pass without a quality optimiser — in which case STOP and report rather than building one here, because that is REPRESENT's job and the V2 boundary says so explicitly.
predictions.P4: Accounting: TOUCH (and page-in) scale with the chosen extent's bits per weight, RESIDENT does not move under canonical decode, and the container's stored footprint is unchanged. FALSIFIED if the ledger only makes sense when resident or stored move too — that would mean extents are really separate objects and the storage design is wrong.
predictions.P5: No executor edits are needed at any depth: the decode realization returns the same shape and the executor cannot tell which extent produced it. FALSIFIED if any `exec/` file outside `tests/` must change for W6 to pass.
predictions.P6: An external crate can register a progressive codec through exported API alone, exactly as `external_codec_provider.rs` does for a terminal one, with no core edits — including its extents reaching selection. FALSIFIED if extent admission requires a match arm anywhere in the planner.

addendum_2026_09_06_boundaries_frozen_be.provenance: Four boundaries stated by the user after the forecast was frozen and before any code was written, plus the implementation order they set. Recorded here so the design decisions they settle are preregistered rather than discovered.

B1_available_requested_selected_are_thre.available_extent: What the ARTIFACT contains — the planes physically present in the container. A terminal progressive artifact holds all three; selecting depth 0 does not make the deeper planes leave the disk, and nothing in the accounting may pretend it does.
B1_available_requested_selected_are_thre.quality_requirement: What EXECUTION must satisfy, expressed representation-independently (a fidelity floor), carried by the plan and the budget. Never a depth: a depth is a fact about one codec, and the semantic plan is hardware- and representation-independent by its own contract (`opplan/planned.rs`).
B1_available_requested_selected_are_thre.selected_extent: What the REALIZATION PIN chooses — the answer selection gives to the requirement, given what the artifact makes available. It lives on the pin, NOT as a mutation of the semantic plan.
B1_available_requested_selected_are_thre.stored_footprint: Every physically present plane, unchanged by whatever extent is selected.
B1_available_requested_selected_are_thre.execution_touch: Only the planes the selected extent requires.
B1_available_requested_selected_are_thre.consequence_for_PlannedOperand_extent: `PlannedOperand.extent` (today always TERMINAL) is a representation-specific depth sitting in a representation-independent structure. It becomes the plan's fidelity REQUIREMENT, or it goes; the depth moves to the pin. Which of the two is decided in implementation and recorded in the notes with the reason.

B2_semantic_ownership_is_not_physical_ow.codec_owns: What 16/24/32-bit depth MEANS; reconstruction at each depth; the fidelity certificate; terminal exactness.
B2_semantic_ownership_is_not_physical_ow.realization_owns: Which streams are touched; whether decoding produces a persistent f32 image; staging and residency; any target-specific direct execution.
B2_semantic_ownership_is_not_physical_ow.rule: Extent SEMANTICS belong to the representation; extent COST belongs to the (representation, realization) pair. This is why touch moves with depth while resident does not under canonical decode, and why a future direct realization over the planes would move resident too without changing a single thing the codec declares.

B3_stream_lengths_are_exact_per_name.rule: Validation states a length per DECLARED STREAM NAME at the requested extent, not a total: `base_hi16` = 2 x elements; `refine_8a` = 1 x elements when depth >= 24; `refine_8b` = 1 x elements when depth = 32. A compensating mutation — base one byte short, a refinement one byte long — MUST refuse, which a total-only rule cannot do (and `lyrw2::bind_region` today checks exactly such a total).
B3_stream_lengths_are_exact_per_name.ordering: Stream order is the codec's declaration order, iterated deterministically; never a map's iteration order. `NamedStreams` is already an insertion-ordered Vec and `streams()` is a static slice — the rule is that binding and validation both walk the DECLARED order, and a test pins it.
B3_stream_lengths_are_exact_per_name.names: `base_hi16`, `refine_8a`, `refine_8b` — the names say the width and the plane, and they are what a refusal prints.

B4_ieee754_edges.plane_order_is_defined_not_inherited: The base plane stores the high 16 bits of the f32 bit pattern as an explicit little-endian u16 (`to_le_bytes`/`from_le_bytes` on the BIT PATTERN), and the refinement planes are single bytes with no endianness at all. Nothing is transmuted from a host float, so the encoding is identical on a big-endian host.
B4_ieee754_edges.terminal: Bit-exact for EVERY pattern: normals, subnormals, +0 and -0, both infinities, and NaNs of any payload. Compared as bit patterns, never as floats, so a NaN whose payload changed is caught.
B4_ieee754_edges.shallow_certified_domain: The declared radius certifies FINITE NORMAL values only. It is a numeric bound and it is checked on that domain (W5).
shallow_defined_but_uncertified: +0 and -0 decode exactly, sign preserved, at every depth.
Both infinities decode exactly at every depth (the exponent field lives entirely in the base plane).
A subnormal truncates toward zero and MAY flush to +/-0 when its significant bits live only in omitted planes — outside any relative bound, which is why the certificate excludes it.

A NaN whose payload exists ONLY in omitted planes decodes as an INFINITY of the same sign: the one case where the pattern's CLASS changes. It is named here, named in the codec's own documentation, and pinned by a test rather than left to be discovered.
B4_ieee754_edges.detection_is_possible_from_the_base_plan: The exponent field is entirely inside `base_hi16`, so a shallow decode can identify non-finite and subnormal-or-zero elements WITHOUT opening a deeper plane. The codec therefore offers a domain check over the base plane; whether a shallow decode merely reports an uncertified domain or REFUSES to certify is the one open decision, and it is decided in implementation and recorded with its reason. What it may never do is decode a NaN into an infinity while claiming a numeric radius.

implementation_order: 2. Terminal bit-exactness over adversarial bit patterns.
3. Monotonic error over finite normal values.
6. Per-stream, per-extent exact-length refusal, including the compensating mutation.
7. Selection pins a depth under a QUALITY requirement plus a throughput constraint.
8. The read witness: deeper sibling tensors were never opened.
9. Accounting: stored footprint unchanged, touch decreases, canonical-f32 residency unchanged.
addendum_2026_09_06_boundaries_frozen_be.selection_test_must_carry_a_quality_requ: Without one the planner trivially picks 16 bits every time and the arm proves nothing. Every selection arm states its floor, and the arm that pins terminal does so BECAUSE of its floor, not because nothing pushed on it.
addendum_2026_09_06_boundaries_frozen_be.exit_claim_restated: One stored representation can expose multiple fidelity extents, and the planner can select how much of it to touch without changing codec semantics or pretending unused refinement bytes do not exist.

not_claimed: No timing, no throughput, no kernel. No claim about quality on a real model: the fidelity here is a property of the ENCODING, certified and checked on fixtures, not a measurement of any checkpoint. No production use of `F32_PLANES` — it is a forcing test for the contract, and its exit is the contract's, not the codec's.
exit_claim: Representation extent and quality are first-class selection dimensions, not format metadata: a codec can offer several extents, the planner can choose one under a budget and refuse when none satisfies the floor, the ledger prices what was chosen, and the deeper streams are never read.
